column1: # habitat_mapping_LDG.tsv — MicrobeAtlas raw environment annotations -> 12 LDG habitat categories
# Manuscript: "Habitat-specific latitudinal diversity gradients in the global microbiome" (v2)
# The Environments field holds pipe-separated two-level strings "main_env;sub_env",
# e.g. "soil;field|animal;human". One row below = one distinct main;sub pair observed
# in the database (65 pairs), with n_samples = number of samples carrying that pair
# (a sample carrying several pairs contributes to several rows; pair-assignments total 1,636,100).
# ASSIGNMENT RULES (exactly as implemented in the analysis; applied per sample over the
# SET of its pairs, plus two side channels: the "f3" field and the "Keywords" field):
#              sub == sediment -> marine_sediment IF pair co-occurs with marine/sea/ocean
#   animal:    gut indication (f3 contains 'gut'/'gastric', or Keywords match
#   urban_built: KEYWORD-DRIVEN ONLY (any env pair): Keywords match
# MULTI-LABEL HANDLING: a sample receives EVERY applicable habitat label (its labels are
# joined with "|" in qc_sample_metadata.csv). In grid aggregation each sample was counted
# once in EACH of its habitats (pandas explode). Consequently the per-habitat sample counts
# in Table 1 of the manuscript sum to 360,868 assignments while unique samples = 352,941.
# Example: "soil;field|animal;human" with gut keywords enters BOTH soil_natural and human_gut.
# UNCLASSIFIED pairs (habitat_LDG = "(unclassified)") were NOT used: e.g. soil;peatland,
# ADDITIONAL SAMPLE FILTERS applied downstream (not part of this mapping):
# experimental-treatment keyword blacklists (tier1/tier2, see manuscript Methods),
# valid coordinates, recomputed Good's coverage >= 0.90 on mapped reads, and
# >= 3 samples per 1x1-degree grid cell per habitat.
